2: Why does the scope matter as much as the policy?
Because Conditional Access for workload identities is narrow, as Microsoft Learn's Conditional Access for workload identities page sets out.
Block is the only grant control.
It covers single-tenant service principals registered in your tenant, and nothing else: not Microsoft or SaaS apps, not multitenant apps, and not managed identities.
A policy assigned to a group that holds a service principal isn't enforced for it; you have to assign the service principal directly.
And Workload I D Premium is needed to create or change these policies.
So in this module you hold the program's two policies, C A oh fifteen for location and C A oh thirty-seven for high risk, as reviewed files.
They're scoped by object I D, one ring at a time, and every one is created report-only.
